text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zambian press on Monday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Deported former UNIP member of the central committee, John Chinula, due to be sent back to Zambia on Monday, may be rendered stateless or be arrested by Zambian immigration authorities who have been investigating hum since 1974 when he allegedly entered he country with documents obtained fraudulently.
Both the Zambia and Malawian government have denied that Chinula is their national and have vowed to kick him out of their respective countries.
- Two UNIP "rebels" who stood as independents have attacked the move to boycott the November 18 elections as blind and counterproductive.

Luena member of parliament Crispen Sibetta and losing candidate for Kafulafuta George Mpombo said in separate interview in Lusaka the decision to withdraw from the race was retrogressive and had left the party in the doldrums.
- The honeymoon for unions with the government is over, Zambia Congress of Trade Unions (ZCTU) president Fackson Shamenda said in Livingstone on Friday.
